content: - [FoodSmart Branding](project_foodsmart_branding.md) — Brand identity, color palette, fonts for the Swedish food waste app

name: FoodSmart Brand Identity
description: Color palette, typography, and design direction for the FoodSmart React Native app (food-app repo)
type: project
---
**Aesthetic**: "Clean Digital Health" — inspired by modern health/wellness apps (soft teal fills, bold heavy sans, light clinical backgrounds).

- **Primary**: `#2E6B65` (deep sage-teal — for buttons, tab active, primary actions)
- **Accent / Hero card fill**: `#5BAAA4` (soft sage teal — fills hero cards with white text on top)
- **Background**: `#EEF1F4` (very light blue-gray — clean, clinical)
- **Success**: `#3DAA6B` (medium green)
- **Danger**: `#E05252` (warm red)
- **Orange/Warning**: `#F59332` (warm amber — for urgency states)

- All fonts are Nunito Sans, heavy weights for headings:
  - `fonts.displayMedium` → `NunitoSans_800ExtraBold` (big headings)
  - `fonts.bodyBold` → `NunitoSans_700Bold`
  - `fonts.bodySemibold` / `fonts.bodyMedium` → `NunitoSans_600SemiBold`
  - `fonts.bodyRegular` → `NunitoSans_400Regular`
  - `fonts.bodyLight` → `NunitoSans_300Light`
- Only `@expo-google-fonts/nunito-sans` is loaded (Lora removed)

- Previously `orange`, `orangeSoft`, `warning` etc. were ALL blue (#2563EB) — completely wrong
- Fixed to proper warm amber colors throughout
- `expiryColor()` in dates.ts updated to match: red → amber → green

- Swedish food waste reduction app ("minska matsvinn")
- Expo 54 / React Native / Expo Router / Supabase backend
- 4 tabs: Hem, Förråd, Recept, Profil
- AI (Claude API) generates recipes from expiring ingredients

Home screen hero card uses `colors.accent` (#5BAAA4 teal) as BACKGROUND fill color with white text — inspired by reference designs. Danger state flips to `colors.danger` red fill. This is the signature visual of the app.

**Why:** User explicitly wants clean, modern, clinical health-app aesthetic (like Hims app, hair analysis app reference). Not warm/earthy. Teal card fills, bold heavy sans, light clean backgrounds.

name: Design style preference
description: User wants Apple-esque clean minimal design - no decorative borders, dashed lines, colored accents. Simple and clean.
type: feedback
---

Keep UI simple, clean, Apple-esque. No decorative/ornamental styling like dashed borders, colored left borders on cards, excessive border treatments. The user described overly-designed UI as "plåttrigt och B" (tacky/ugly).

**Why:** User has strong aesthetic preference for minimalism. Decorative elements like border-d

- React compiler strict: No `any`, no refs during render, no setState in effects
- Fix for setState-in-effect: Use lazy state initializers, `useSyncExternalStore`, or eslint-disable
- Fix for impure render: Use `useId()` instead of `Math.random()`
- Component naming: Default export functions MUST be PascalCase for hooks rules
- Supabase `Json` columns: cast with proper interfaces, not `any`
- Build command: `npm run build`, lint: `npm run lint` (0 errors required)

- `ai_jobs` has NO FK to books — `bookId` is stored in `input` JSONB column
- `chapter_audio_cache` has no FK to books (linked via chapter_id)
- Most book-related tables use ON DELETE CASCADE from books: chapters, book_versions, audiobook_assets, marketing_campaigns, translations
- `book_imports.book_id` uses ON DELETE SET NULL (leaves orphans)
- Admin client: `createAdminClient()` from `@/lib/supabase/admin` (service role, bypasses RLS)

- Next.js 16 App Router, Supabase (no Prisma), BullMQ jobs, Tailwind
- Auth: `requireAuthorRoleForApi()` from `@/lib/auth/require-author`
- Admin auth: `checkAdmin()` from `@/lib/admin-auth` (timing-safe comparison, rate-limited)
- Feature flags: `@/lib/flags` (audiobook, translations, marketing, discovery)
- English-first policy for reader/public pages (enforced by `check:english-default` CI). Swedish only in author dashboard.

- `npm run qa:beta` — 7 stages: env → tests → lint → english-default → no-placeholders → dead-code → build
- All stages must pass before beta release

name: Strict Design System Rules
description: User-defined design system that MUST be followed for all Verkli UI work. No freestyle design allowed.
type: feedback
---

Never "design freely" — always follow the strict Verkli design system.

**Why:** User explicitly mandated this after I introduced custom hex colors, random spacing, custom shadows, and gradient blobs that made the app look inconsistent and broken. The goal is a cohesive, premium product — not random components.

**How to apply:**

- Purple: #907AFF
- Background: #F8F9FB
- Surface: #FFFFFF
- Border: rgba(0,0,0,0.06)
- Text primary: #0F172A
- Text secondary: #64748B
- States: green-500, amber-500, red-500

- Heading XL: text-3xl font-semibold
- Heading L: text-2xl font-semibold
- Heading M: text-xl font-semibold
- Body: text-sm
- Meta: text-xs
- NO custom px like text-[13px]

- Gaps: gap-2, gap-4, gap-6, gap-8
- Padding: p-4 (small), p-6 (standard), p-8 (large)
- No random spacing

- rounded-xl (default)
- rounded-2xl (large containers)

- Card: shadow-sm
- Elevated: shadow-md
- White bg, subtle border, NO gradients

- Primary: solid purple
- Secondary: outline
- Ghost: text only

- Header (title + primary action) → Content sections → Clear grouping
- max-w-5xl or max-w-6xl

- No new colors
- No random spacing
- No inline styles
- No custom shadows (like shadow-[0_4px_24px_...])
- No gradient backgrounds on cards
- No mixing visual styles

File: `src/lib/author-locale.tsx`

```
library.title
library.subtitle
library.emptyTitle
library.emptyBody
production.emptyTitle
production.emptyBody
production.createBook
production.sectionTitle
production.sectionBody
```

- Only add a key if it's actually used in JSX via `t("key")`. Twice during cleanup, dead keys (`library.createBook`, `library.newBook`) accumulated — they were removed.
- "New book" strings in LibraryWorkspace are hardcoded (not locale keys) because the button label never needs translation in the author dashboard (English-first policy for author UI is inconsistent, but this is the current state).
- The hook `useAuthorLocale()` detects browser locale and falls back to EN. Swedish authors get Swed

name: Author Dashboard UX Cleanup Patterns
description: Established patterns from two QA passes — what was removed, what replaced it, and why
type: feedback
---

- **Growth percentages on StatsCards** — removed because no time-series data exists. Don't add fake "↑12%" badges.
- **DashboardFilter component** — removed because it was decorative (no backend filtering). Don't add filter UI without backend support.
- **"sv-SE" hardcoded locale** — replaced with `toLocaleDateString(undefined, {...})` everywhere. Always use `undefined` as locale to respect system locale.
- **Multiple CreateBookDialog instances** — LibraryWorkspace previously had 3 separate dial

Two heading styles in use — use the right one:
- **Dashboard/workspace page title**: `text-[17px] font-medium uppercase tracking-[0.14em] text-[#8B92A5]` (faint, muted — Dashboard page only)
- **Named workspace page title**: `text-[22px] font-semibold tracking-tight text-slate-900 dark:text-white` (bold, prominent — Library, Profile, Production)

**Why:** The user called out Profile using the old faint style as a bug during QA pass 2.

Save buttons go at the BOTTOM of forms, not the top. The profile page had it at top — moved to bottom.

**Why:** Standard form UX. User sees what they're saving before the submit action.

Editor pages show breadcrumb `Library / Book Title` instead of a flat title. Both clickable. "View as reader ↗" appears in headerRight for published books (opens `/reader/books/${bookId}` in new tab).
"Switch to reader" renamed to "Open reader app" — it's not switching modes, it's opening a different app experience.
